types.name: Client
types.description:
A client is a way of authenticating users with a release.
 The strategy of authentication is defined by the kind of client. And allows for different authentication flow. 
 E.g a client can be a DESKTOP app, that might be used by multiple users, or a WEBSITE that wants to connect to a user's account, 
 but also a DEVELOPMENT client that is used by a developer to test the app. The client model thinly wraps the oauth2 client model, which is used to authenticate users.

fields.name: clientId
fields.description: The OAuth2 client id this client authenticates as.

fields.name: functional
fields.description: Is this client functional? A functional client is a client that is able to authenticate users. If a client is not functional, it will not be able to authenticate users.

fields.name: issueUrl
fields.description: The issue url of the client. This is the url where users can report issues and get more information about the client.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: What kind of principal this client is (its authentication strategy): DEVELOPMENT, WEBSITE, DESKTOP, MOBILE, HUB or RELYING_PARTY.

fields.name: logo
fields.description: The logo of the release. This should be a url to a logo that can be used to represent the release.

fields.name: mappings
fields.description: The mappings of the client. A mapping is a mapping of a service to a service instance. This is used to configure the hub.

fields.name: name
fields.description: A human-readable label for the client that folds in the app, version, operator and device — e.g. `com.example.app:v0.1.1 by Johannes on my-laptop`.

fields.name: node
fields.description: The node this runs on

fields.name: public
fields.description: Is this client public? A public client cannot keep a secret (desktop apps, mobile apps, SPAs, hub identities) and authenticates without one, relying on PKCE / device-code flows instead.

fields.name: publicSources
fields.description: The public sources of the client. These are the public sources where users can find more information about the client.

fields.name: release
fields.description: The release that this client belongs to. Null for clients that are not bound to an app release (hub identities, relying parties, pending registrations).

fields.name: role
fields.description: The operational role of the client. INTERFACE clients are human interfaces operated by a user in real time. AGENT clients are authorized once and then run unattended, receiving and processing tasks on the user's behalf.

fields.name: user
fields.description: The user this client acts for (derived from its membership).

types.name: ClientFilter
types.description:
The one client model: every OAuth2 principal is a row here.

Kinds of rows and their lifecycle:

- **App clients** (`development`/`website`/`desktop`/`mobile`): the row is created by
  dynamic registration at ``/o/app-authorization/`` with identity fields
  only; human approval *binds* it (membership, organization, release, hub,
  mappings, scope). ``membership`` null == not yet approved.
- **Hub identities** (`hub`): same lifecycle via ``/o/hub-authorization/``;
  the created ``Hub`` links back via ``Hub.client`` (reverse:
  ``client.hub_identity``).
- **Relying parties** (`relying_party`): confidential OIDC clients
  provisioned from config by ``ensureopenid``; global (no organization).

Implements authlib's ``ClientMixin`` directly — there is no separate
OAuth2 client table anymore.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

args.description: Explains why this element was deprecated, usually also including a suggestion for how to access supported similar data. Formatted using the Markdown syntax, as specified by [CommonMark](https://commonmark.org/).
